newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada February retail sales rise 1.1 percent.
newsitem.headline: Canada February retail sales rise 1.1 percent.

text.p: Canadian retail sales rose 1.1 percent in February to a seasonally adjusted C$19.09 billion from a revised C$18.89 billion (C$18.79 billion) in January, Statistics Canada said on Tuesday.
Sales, ex vehicles, s/a +1.3 +7.9 C$14.50 bln
Statistics Canada said early indications for March sales were for an increase in the number of new motor vehicles sold.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a 0.9 percent rise in retail sales in February after January's revised 1.0 percent rise.

While the automotive sector drove retail sales in late 1996, sales increases in the first two months of 1997 were more broadly based, Statistics Canada said. Lower interest rates in 1996 may have made the purchase of big-ticket items more attractive to consumers, the federal agency said.
Consumers spent more in February compared to January in each of the seven retail trade sectors, the agency said.

Sales from general merchandise stores rose 3.7 percent, including a 2.4 percent advance in deparment store sales for the month. Automotive sector sales were up 1.0 percent, led by sales in auto parts and accessoires, while furniture store sales rose 2.0 percent.
These three sectors -- general merchandise, automotive and furniture stores -- accounted for more than 80 percent of the February increase, StatsCan said.

In British Columbia, retailers saw a 3.1 percent decline in sales in February from artificially high levels recorded in January. Sales in the western province slowed in December because of major snowstorms, prompting a buying spree in January, the agency said.
Excluding British Columbia, total retail sales in Canada increased by 1.5 percent in February.
(For more information from Statistics Canada, contact the Retail Trade Section, Industry Division, Greg Peterson at 613- 951-3592.)
